summary: Eleven labels print rosemary extract 500 mg and two print rosemary leaf 700 mg, with no positioning category. One study meets the reading bar: a sponsor-funded 4-week crossover in 40 healthy adults with 200 mg/day of an extract standardized to rosmarinic acid and diterpenes, where trait anxiety on the STAI, its stated primary outcome, improved versus placebo while cortisol and VAS scores did not differ (41312013). Other oral trials are small, in different populations, and name no primary outcome in the abstract: COPD (37758539), students (29389474), major depression as an adjunct (36343423), fatty liver disease, null versus placebo at 4 g (35318738). The stored trial is single doses with benefit at 750 mg and impairment at 6,000 mg (21877951). Only 41312013 was read in full text passages; the others are abstracts only.

population.description: 40 healthy Japanese adults aged 20 to 60 who reported daily stress, in the crossover study.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial with a 4-week washout, after a separate 4-week open-label safety study in 22 adults

outcomes.name: Trait anxiety on the STAI improved after 4 weeks versus placebo

limitations: One small crossover in healthy adults; no clinical anxiety population.

Numeric between-group results and the analyzed count were not extracted.
